source: 12 Fortinet feature/admin guide lessons; Community secondary scenario context

questions.stem: A hub negotiates IKE_SA_INIT, but a new tunnel stalls before IKE_AUTH after enabling PQC. Which comparison is decisive?

choices.text: Compare both peers' phase-1 additional KE groups and exchange support.
choices.feedback: IKE_INTERMEDIATE proposals must agree before authentication can finish.

choices.text: Compare firewall policy sequence numbers on the affected inside interfaces.
choices.feedback: Forward policy ordering does not negotiate additional IKE keys.

choices.text: Compare ESP traffic counters after clearing the active tunnel.
choices.feedback: ESP counters are downstream and may remain zero after negotiation fails.

choices.text: Compare DNS resolver cache entries for the peer hostname.
choices.feedback: DNS cache may affect reachability but not a negotiated KE mismatch.

questions.stem: IKEv2 is established, but a new CHILD_SA fails following phase-2 PQC changes. Where should diagnosis start?

choices.text: Review the FortiGate's global web proxy certificate settings.
choices.feedback: Proxy certificates do not determine CHILD_SA additional KE compatibility.

choices.text: Review both phase-2 addke proposals and FOLLOWUP_KE behavior.
choices.feedback: CHILD_SA rekey/additional KE can differ from the established IKE SA.

choices.text: Review the switch's 802.1X port authorization counters.
choices.feedback: 802.1X controls local access rather than IKE phase-2 negotiation.

choices.text: Review the FortiAnalyzer report retention and roll schedule.
choices.feedback: Log retention cannot cause a phase-2 KEM proposal mismatch.

questions.stem: A tunnel's ESP counters increase after a PQC rollout. What is still unproven?

choices.text: Whether the firewall rule permits all production destinations.
choices.feedback: ESP counts alone do not prove every destination policy.

choices.text: Whether the peer can route return traffic through the tunnel.
choices.feedback: ESP counts alone do not show return-path reachability.

choices.text: Whether the negotiated SA used the intended additional KEM.
choices.feedback: Data-plane counters cannot attest to the negotiated addke group.

choices.text: Whether the WAN MTU can carry ordinary encrypted packets.
choices.feedback: Packets can pass without proving all larger MTU cases.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to enable PQC on seven spoke tunnels in one change. Which staged test best reduces negotiation risk?

choices.text: Increase DPD retries and assume KEM compatibility follows.
choices.feedback: DPD timing does not establish cryptographic group support.

choices.text: Enable all additional KE rounds on every spoke immediately.
choices.feedback: A simultaneous rollout hides which peer proposal first fails.

choices.text: Enable only ESP encryption changes and skip peer checks.
choices.feedback: ESP cipher changes do not verify IKE additional exchanges.

choices.text: Test a compatible pair, verify exchanges, then stage spokes.
choices.feedback: A pilot verifies compatibility and rekey behavior before scale.

questions.stem: FortiManager shows no DHCP Discover in a scheduled FortiSwitch PCAP. What should be checked first?

choices.text: Selected switch, ingress port, filter and capture time window.
choices.feedback: An empty capture is ambiguous until observation scope and time are correct.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer's archive file rolling interval and quota.
choices.feedback: Archive retention does not determine FortiSwitch capture visibility.

choices.text: The WAN SD-WAN SLA target and current FortiGuard license status.
choices.feedback: WAN probe entitlement is unrelated to a local switch capture.

choices.text: The wireless MPSK profile's SAE transition security type.
choices.feedback: MPSK mode is not the first explanation for a mis-scoped PCAP.

questions.stem: A FortiManager capture contains RADIUS Access-Accept for a wired endpoint. What cannot yet be concluded?

choices.text: The RADIUS server returned an affirmative authentication decision.
choices.feedback: The packet directly shows the RADIUS response decision.

choices.text: The access switch installed the authorized VLAN on its port.
choices.feedback: An Access-Accept does not prove hardware VLAN assignment.

choices.text: The management workflow captured a packet at that interface.
choices.feedback: The observed packet confirms capture operation at that point.

choices.text: The upstream path carried a response toward the access switch.
choices.feedback: The observed packet supports upstream response transport.

questions.stem: An intermittent outage occurs only at 03:00. Which FortiManager capability most directly preserves evidence?

choices.text: A FortiGate firewall policy comparison from last week.
choices.feedback: Policy diffs cannot show which frames arrived at 03:00.

choices.text: An ADOM object deletion report after the outage.
choices.feedback: Object deletion history does not capture the transient packet path.

choices.text: A scheduled switch packet capture covering the outage.
choices.feedback: Scheduled PCAPs observe transient traffic during the failure window.

choices.text: A full FortiAnalyzer backup performed during business hours.
choices.feedback: A backup does not record the packet exchange causing the outage.

questions.stem: A FortiManager PCAP shows DHCP Discover but no Offer. What is the next sound isolation step?

choices.text: Replace all client MPSK keys across the WLAN.
choices.feedback: Rotating WLAN keys is unrelated to an observed DHCP Discover.

choices.text: Clear the FortiSIEM ClickHouse event database.
choices.feedback: SIEM event storage does not affect DHCP server replies.

choices.text: Immediately disable the FortiGate's DoS anomaly policy.
choices.feedback: DoS policy is unproven and may not govern this VLAN.

choices.text: Capture at the uplink or FortiGate DHCP boundary.
choices.feedback: Moving the capture boundary localizes where the reply disappears.

questions.stem: FortiAnalyzer reports archive data older than its 90-day setting. Which mechanism explains this?

choices.text: File-level retention waits until all records are out of window.
choices.feedback: Mixed-age rolled files remain until the entire file is eligible.

choices.text: Each individual archive record is deleted at midnight on expiry.
choices.feedback: Archive deletion is file-granular, not per-record at midnight.

choices.text: A report SQL dataset overrides archive deletion dates.
choices.feedback: Report datasets cannot alter archive file deletion granularity.

choices.text: The log forwarding connector always duplicates old records.
choices.feedback: Forwarding may copy logs but does not explain file eligibility.

questions.stem: An ADOM's log rate is normal but a historical report lacks one day. What does rate evidence prove?

choices.text: All historical archive files remain present and searchable.
choices.feedback: Current rate cannot attest to old archive completeness.

choices.text: Current log ingestion exists, not continuous historical retention.
choices.feedback: The command observes current ADOM ingestion, not file retention.

choices.text: All log files have been rolled precisely every 24 hours.
choices.feedback: Daily rolling must be separately configured and verified.

choices.text: The report's SQL query has no time-filter defects.
choices.feedback: A rate counter does not validate report query filters.

questions.stem: A low-volume ADOM has compressed files spanning several days. Which change targets deletion granularity?

choices.text: Increase the file size threshold to several gigabytes.
choices.feedback: Larger files generally span more days at low volume.

choices.text: Disable analytics indexing while keeping archive unchanged.
choices.feedback: Indexing does not change file-level archive roll boundaries.

choices.text: Configure scheduled daily rolling for bounded file spans.
choices.feedback: Daily rolling keeps files near day boundaries for retention.

choices.text: Move the ADOM to a different FortiManager workspace.
choices.feedback: FortiManager workspaces are unrelated to FAZ archive files.

questions.stem: Storage-size pressure removes logs from days 60–89 while day 90 survives. Why might that occur?

choices.text: A new report dataset created a gap in the raw logs.
choices.feedback: Datasets cannot create archive retention gaps by themselves.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer automatically replays missing archived days.
choices.feedback: Retention does not automatically replay missing log history.

choices.text: Every record is deleted in strict chronological timestamp order.
choices.feedback: The deletion unit is a file, not an individual record.

choices.text: Whole-file deletion follows the oldest last-received log.
choices.feedback: Deleting whole files can leave non-contiguous date coverage.

questions.stem: A FortiSwitch ingress ACL appears in configuration but packets still pass. What evidence matters next?

choices.text: Assigned ACL group, hardware usage, action and match counters.
choices.feedback: Hardware enforcement requires attachment, support and matching action.

choices.text: FortiGate's central NAT policy and translated address pool selection.
choices.feedback: Central NAT does not program a FortiSwitch ingress ACL.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer's report scheduling and analytics disk quota.
choices.feedback: Reporting storage is downstream of switch hardware decisions.

choices.text: FortiSASE administrator comments for last month's edits.
choices.feedback: Audit comments do not prove switch ASIC policy installation.

questions.stem: An ACL match counter rises but traffic is not blocked. Which explanation fits the evidence?

choices.text: The ACL must be acting as a FortiGate firewall policy.
choices.feedback: A switch ACL is not a FortiGate forwarding policy.

choices.text: The matching ACL action may count or remark, not drop.
choices.feedback: A match can trigger non-drop actions such as counting or remarking.

choices.text: The switch's MCLAG heartbeat necessarily went down.
choices.feedback: MCLAG failure is not implied by ACL counter behavior.

choices.text: The client must have received a different MPSK key.
choices.feedback: MPSK key assignment does not determine wired ACL action.

questions.stem: A switch in ACL density mode loses free entries after deleting rules. What is the documented remedy boundary?

choices.text: Change the FortiManager ADOM's policy revision status.
choices.feedback: ADOM revisions do not release switch density-mode allocation.

choices.text: Run FortiNAC portal Publish to reload all access rules.
choices.feedback: FortiNAC web rules do not reclaim switch ACL hardware.

choices.text: Plan ACL key-compaction or switch restart with disruption awareness.
choices.feedback: Density-mode hardware resources may need compaction or restart.

choices.text: Disable the FortiGate's IPsec childless IKE negotiation.
choices.feedback: IKE negotiation has no bearing on ACL TCAM reclamation.

questions.stem: A managed FortiSwitch supports ingress ACLs but a configured action fails on one model. What is most likely?

choices.text: The RADIUS shared secret must be regenerated first.
choices.feedback: RADIUS secrets are unrelated to a hardware ACL action.

choices.text: The DHCP relay agent is suppressing policy download.
choices.feedback: DHCP relay does not govern switch ACL ASIC capability.

choices.text: All switches support identical actions after FortiManager install.
choices.feedback: ACL action support differs by switch family and release.

choices.text: The model-specific ACL feature matrix restricts that action.
choices.feedback: The guide explicitly documents model-specific classifier/action limits.

questions.stem: Two MPSK clients associate to one SSID but land in different VLANs. What determines that split?

choices.text: The matched MPSK key/group's dynamic VLAN configuration.
choices.feedback: MPSK maps matched credentials to group/VLAN authorization.

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer archive retention policy for each client.
choices.feedback: Log retention has no role in WLAN VLAN assignment.

choices.text: The SD-WAN rule's chosen underlay health-check target.
choices.feedback: WAN health checks occur after local WLAN segmentation.

choices.text: The FortiPAM secret checkout duration for the administrator.
choices.feedback: PAM checkout does not select client WLAN VLANs.

questions.stem: After enabling MPSK, a legacy client loses DHCP although association succeeds. Which path is most relevant?

choices.text: The FortiGate's IKEv2 additional KE group proposal and peer compatibility.
choices.feedback: IKE KEM negotiation is unrelated to WLAN DHCP.

choices.text: The key-selected VLAN's tagging, DHCP and policy path.
choices.feedback: MPSK enables dynamic VLAN; L3 reachability must be revalidated.

choices.text: The FortiSIEM region's ClickHouse shard placement.
choices.feedback: SIEM storage placement does not provide DHCP service.

choices.text: The FortiAuthenticator OAuth token refresh expiry value.
choices.feedback: OAuth refresh tokens do not determine WPA association VLANs.

questions.stem: An SSID is configured for WPA3 SAE-only keys, but an older WPA2 client fails. Which mismatch should be examined?

choices.text: FortiManager's scheduled switch capture duration.
choices.feedback: Capture duration does not change client cipher capability.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer's compressed log file roll trigger and archive retention policy.
choices.feedback: Archive roll triggers do not control WLAN authentication.

choices.text: The MPSK security mode versus the client's WPA capability.
choices.feedback: SAE-only key types may exclude WPA2-only supplicants.

choices.text: FortiSASE's required administrator change-summary field.
choices.feedback: Audit comments do not change WPA3 key negotiation.

questions.stem: A team assigns two MPSK profiles to one VAP and expects both to apply. What is the documented limit?

choices.text: Both profiles apply if they share the same security type.
choices.feedback: Matching security types do not bypass the one-profile limit.

choices.text: The controller merges profiles after the next FortiAP reboot.
choices.feedback: A reboot does not change the VAP association model.

choices.text: Two profiles combine only when DHCP snooping is enabled.
choices.feedback: DHCP snooping does not merge MPSK profiles.

choices.text: Only one MPSK profile can be bound to a VAP.
choices.feedback: The guide explicitly restricts VAPs to one MPSK profile.

questions.stem: A FortiNAC portal rule was edited but browsers still follow the old redirect. What was likely omitted?

choices.text: Publishing the rule set to restart the portal HTTP process.
choices.feedback: Stored edits are not active until portal rules are published.

choices.text: Updating the FortiGate's SD-WAN FortiGuard preset database.
choices.feedback: SD-WAN presets do not change captive portal HTTP routing.

choices.text: Rebuilding the FortiSwitch ingress ACL hardware key table during maintenance.
choices.feedback: Switch ACL key compaction is unrelated to portal redirects.

choices.text: Refreshing FortiSIEM's ClickHouse shard membership map.
choices.feedback: SIEM storage regions do not affect the portal HTTP process.

questions.stem: A FortiNAC request matcher uses `example.com` as regex. What subtle problem can arise?

choices.text: It automatically matches only exact hostname bytes.
choices.feedback: Regex dot is not an exact literal by default.

choices.text: The dot can match any character without escaping.
choices.feedback: Unescaped dot matches any single character in regex.

choices.text: It can only match an HTTP User Agent, never a URI.
choices.feedback: Rules can match Request URI or HTTP User Agent.

choices.text: It is interpreted as a RADIUS attribute rather than regex.
choices.feedback: Request Processing Rules inspect HTTP fields, not RADIUS attributes.

questions.stem: A portal shows 102 Request Processing Rules instead of 51. What first action is justified?

choices.text: Disable portal service logging and restart the appliance.
choices.feedback: Disabling logs removes evidence without finding duplicates.

choices.text: Delete half the records using an unreviewed SQL command.
choices.feedback: Unreviewed database deletion risks portal configuration integrity.

choices.text: Identify duplicate matcher/action/target groups before changes.
choices.feedback: Grouping rule fields exposes duplicates for controlled remediation.

choices.text: Replace all registration VLANs to clear stale browser cache.
choices.feedback: VLAN changes do not resolve duplicated portal HTTP rules.

questions.stem: A captive portal's HTTP request is redirected correctly but endpoint registration fails. What is the correct inference?

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer report database must be out of sync.
choices.feedback: FortiAnalyzer reporting does not control registration workflow.

choices.text: The client has certainly completed all post-login compliance checks.
choices.feedback: The browser redirect is earlier than compliance completion.

choices.text: The portal HTTP rules also proved RADIUS VLAN authorization.
choices.feedback: A redirect does not prove access policy or registration success.

choices.text: HTTP request routing works; inspect downstream registration stages.
choices.feedback: The request-rule layer can succeed while registration later fails.

questions.stem: A FortiNAC-F operator attempts a Winbind domain join against FreeIPA and gets a join error. Which design fact matters?

choices.text: Winbind performs an AD-style Samba join for MSCHAPv2.
choices.feedback: The Samba AD join requirement explains the FreeIPA incompatibility.

choices.text: Winbind authenticates any LDAP directory through STARTTLS.
choices.feedback: The guide says Winbind cannot encrypt with LDAPS/STARTTLS.

choices.text: Winbind requires a FortiSASE security PoP for each domain.
choices.feedback: SASE PoPs do not participate in FortiNAC domain joining.

choices.text: Winbind is used only for EAP-TLS certificate chain checks.
choices.feedback: EAP-TLS does not require the Winbind MSCHAPv2 path.

questions.stem: An endpoint uses EAP-TLS and Winbind shows Not Joined. What should the engineer conclude?

choices.text: All EAP-TLS authentications must be rejected by Winbind.
choices.feedback: EAP-TLS is not the Winbind authentication path.

choices.text: The certificate path can work independently of Winbind.
choices.feedback: Fortinet documents Winbind as specific to MSCHAPv2.

choices.text: The FortiGate must disable TLS certificate inspection globally.
choices.feedback: FortiGate TLS inspection is unrelated to this EAP method.

choices.text: The endpoint requires a shared MSCHAPv2 machine password.
choices.feedback: Certificate authentication does not require MSCHAPv2 secrets.

questions.stem: Winbind shows stale domain details but Not Joined and a 1970 machine-password date. Which evidence should dominate?

choices.text: The RADIUS client MAC address and access-switch model.
choices.feedback: Client MAC and switch model cannot establish Winbind join state.

choices.text: The previously displayed domain-controller hostname alone.
choices.feedback: A cached controller name is not proof of active domain trust.

choices.text: Current join status and machine-account lifecycle indicators.
choices.feedback: The guide warns stale details and epoch dates indicate lost join.

choices.text: The user's browser captive-portal redirect target URL.
choices.feedback: Portal redirects are outside the MSCHAPv2 directory trust boundary.

questions.stem: A second AD domain was added to Winbind, but MSCHAPv2 works only for the first. What should be checked?

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer log rolling threshold and archive quota.
choices.feedback: Archive retention does not validate an AD domain join.

choices.text: FortiSwitch ingress ACL density mode and current TCAM usage limits.
choices.feedback: Switch ACL resources do not determine Winbind trust.

choices.text: FortiPAM secret launcher TOTP duration and hash.
choices.feedback: PAM TOTP does not determine directory discovery.

choices.text: DNS A/SRV records and the second Winbind instance's join.
choices.feedback: Additional domains require DNS and separate working Winbind configuration.

questions.stem: A public OAuth client sends an authorization code but token exchange fails after a page reload. Which state is essential?

choices.text: The original PKCE verifier matching the submitted challenge.
choices.feedback: The verifier binds code redemption to the initiating client.

choices.text: The FortiSwitch ACL ingress policy assigned to the client.
choices.feedback: Switch ACL assignment is unrelated to OAuth code redemption.

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer active archive file's roll timestamp.
choices.feedback: Archive timestamps do not affect token verifier matching.

choices.text: The SD-WAN health check's FortiGuard predefined name.
choices.feedback: SD-WAN presets do not validate OAuth token requests.

questions.stem: A developer adds a client_secret to fix FortiAuthenticator PKCE authorization errors. Why is this ineffective?

choices.text: PKCE requires a privileged FortiGate firewall policy first.
choices.feedback: FortiGate policy is not the missing PKCE proof.

choices.text: The public PKCE flow ignores client_secret for this request.
choices.feedback: FortiAuthenticator documents client_secret ignored for PKCE authorization.

choices.text: OAuth requires an LDAP machine-account Winbind domain join.
choices.feedback: Winbind MSCHAPv2 is not required for OAuth PKCE.

choices.text: The secret is validated only after a FortiPAM session starts.
choices.feedback: PAM session state does not validate OAuth public clients.

questions.stem: An authorization request is rejected before user login. Which PKCE fields are explicitly required?

choices.text: A FortiSASE change-summary string and event-log filter.
choices.feedback: Audit comments are not PKCE request parameters.

choices.text: An ESP cipher proposal and phase-2 addke group list.
choices.feedback: IKEv2 proposal data is not an OAuth request field.

choices.text: A code_challenge and code_challenge_method in authorization.
choices.feedback: The documented endpoint requires both challenge and method.

choices.text: A FortiAnalyzer report dataset and archive roll time.
choices.feedback: Report datasets are unrelated to OAuth request validation.

questions.stem: A callback receives a code at an unexpected HTTP redirect URI. What configuration control is most relevant?

choices.text: FortiNAC portal Request Processing Rules publication status.
choices.feedback: FortiNAC portal rules are not FortiAuthenticator RP policy.

choices.text: FortiAP MPSK dynamic VLAN and WPA3 transition mode.
choices.feedback: MPSK segmentation is separate from OAuth redirects.

choices.text: FortiSIEM ClickHouse worker region membership and shard.
choices.feedback: SIEM region routing does not validate OAuth callback URIs.

choices.text: FortiAuthenticator allowed redirect URIs and HTTPS preference.
choices.feedback: The RP explicitly registers redirect URIs; HTTPS is recommended.

questions.stem: An SSH target requests TOTP, but WebSSH cannot complete authentication after a method change. What should be verified?

choices.text: Whether the target still offers keyboard-interactive authentication.
choices.feedback: WebSSH TOTP is documented to require keyboard-interactive.

choices.text: Whether the FortiGuard SLA preset license has expired.
choices.feedback: WAN probe licensing does not determine SSH auth methods.

choices.text: Whether the FortiSwitch ACL is configured for density mode.
choices.feedback: ACL density mode does not govern SSH OTP delivery.

choices.text: Whether FortiAnalyzer uses weekly instead of daily rolling.
choices.feedback: Archive rolling does not affect PAM launcher authentication.

questions.stem: A FortiPAM secret inherits an eight-digit TOTP template, but its target expects six digits. What fixes the mismatch?

choices.text: Change FortiAuthenticator OAuth token expiry to six hours.
choices.feedback: OAuth expiry does not change a target TOTP code length.

choices.text: Override the secret's TOTP length and verify interval/hash.
choices.feedback: Per-secret override can align length, duration and hash.

choices.text: Disable the FortiNAC portal request-rule publish operation.
choices.feedback: Portal publishing does not generate privileged SSH OTPs.

choices.text: Increase the FortiSIEM Event Upload Worker shard count.
choices.feedback: SIEM storage scaling does not alter TOTP calculations.

questions.stem: A non-proxy FortiPAM web launcher never auto-enters the target OTP. What is the documented behavior?

choices.text: It silently disables the target's second factor requirement.
choices.feedback: A launcher cannot simply disable target-enforced MFA.

choices.text: It always falls back to an IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange.
choices.feedback: IKEv2 exchanges are unrelated to browser OTP filling.

choices.text: Some non-proxy/web launches require manual TOTP entry.
choices.feedback: The guide identifies manual code entry for unsupported launchers.

choices.text: It automatically enrolls a new FortiToken for every session.
choices.feedback: FortiToken enrollment is not automatically performed per session.

questions.stem: A correct FortiPAM TOTP seed intermittently fails every few attempts. Which measurement is most informative?

choices.text: The switch port's VLAN and ACL match counter values.
choices.feedback: Switch ACL counters do not explain generated code mismatch.

choices.text: The FortiSASE administrator audit summary retention age.
choices.feedback: Audit retention does not determine OTP code validity.

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer per-ADOM log volume and archive age.
choices.feedback: Archive metrics cannot validate OTP time windows.

choices.text: Target/PAM clock skew versus TOTP step duration and hash.
choices.feedback: TOTP depends on synchronized time and matching code parameters.

questions.stem: FortiSIEM collectors upload successfully but a tenant's events land in the wrong ClickHouse shard. What should be inspected?

choices.text: Collector worker destinations and region-to-shard assignments.
choices.feedback: Storage regions route events through designated workers to shards.

choices.text: FortiPAM secret template TOTP shared-key encoding.
choices.feedback: PAM TOTP cannot affect SIEM event placement.

choices.text: FortiAP MPSK group assignment and SAE password type.
choices.feedback: WLAN PSK assignment does not select ClickHouse shards.

choices.text: FortiGate IPsec phase-2 traffic selectors and proposals.
choices.feedback: IPsec selectors are not FortiSIEM worker placement policy.

questions.stem: A load balancer sends all collectors to workers across two FortiSIEM storage regions. What is the design flaw?

choices.text: Regions require every collector to use all available workers.
choices.feedback: Region isolation requires destination-aware routing, not all workers.

choices.text: Collector traffic should reach workers in its intended region.
choices.feedback: The documented region architecture requires correct worker targeting.

choices.text: ClickHouse data nodes must overlap between every region.
choices.feedback: The guide requires non-overlapping shards and workers.

choices.text: Event forwarding must bypass all load balancers in 7.5.
choices.feedback: Load balancers are supported when region routing is configured.

questions.stem: A ClickHouse node reports DUPLICATE_DATA_PART. Which response respects the diagnostic boundary?

choices.text: Disable FortiSASE administrator change comments temporarily.
choices.feedback: Audit comments do not affect ClickHouse storage integrity.

choices.text: Change the FortiNAC RADIUS VLAN to trigger new events.
choices.feedback: NAC VLAN changes cannot repair ClickHouse data parts.

choices.text: Inspect database service/logs before any supported repair.
choices.feedback: Storage-engine errors need service/log evidence and safe recovery.

choices.text: Reassign every collector to a different region immediately.
choices.feedback: Worker reassignment does not repair a duplicate database part.

questions.stem: An event is visible at a FortiSIEM Event Upload Worker but absent from searches. What is still unproven?

choices.text: Whether the worker received any packet from the sender.
choices.feedback: The worker observation already supports packet arrival.

choices.text: Whether the source emitted a log during the time window.
choices.feedback: A received event supports source emission for that record.

choices.text: Whether the collector established a transport connection.
choices.feedback: The worker observation already supports transport receipt.

choices.text: Whether the expected shard committed and indexed the event.
choices.feedback: Worker receipt is upstream of shard persistence and query visibility.

questions.stem: A FortiSASE administrator edits a traffic policy but the change is not saved until a dialog is completed. What feature may be active?

choices.text: Mandatory configuration-audit change-summary comments.
choices.feedback: FortiSASE can gate changes on submitting a comment.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer archive log rolling at a scheduled time.
choices.feedback: Archive rolling does not block SASE policy saves.

choices.text: FortiSwitch density-mode ACL key compaction control.
choices.feedback: Switch ACL compaction is unrelated to portal audit prompts.

choices.text: FortiAuthenticator OAuth public-client PKCE enforcement.
choices.feedback: OAuth PKCE is unrelated to administrator edit comments.

questions.stem: A reviewer requests a FortiSASE change comment from 45 days ago. What is the documented limitation?

choices.text: All change summaries are immutable for seven years.
choices.feedback: The guide does not promise seven-year summary retention.

choices.text: Existing change summaries are retained for 30 days.
choices.feedback: Fortinet documents a 30-day retention for change summaries.

choices.text: Only FortiManager can export SASE audit information.
choices.feedback: The guide does not require FortiManager to review events.

choices.text: The audit setting records no administrator identity.
choices.feedback: Administrator identity is part of the change summary log.

questions.stem: A policy appears effective, but its new Administrator Event is not immediately visible. What should the engineer account for?

choices.text: FortiNAC portal web-server publish restart duration.
choices.feedback: NAC web publishing does not determine SASE audit timing.

choices.text: FortiGate IKEv2 post-quantum rekey timing and groups.
choices.feedback: IKE rekey is unrelated to audit-event ingestion latency.

choices.text: Possible delay before FortiSASE audit logs appear.
choices.feedback: The guide warns new Administrator Events can appear later.

choices.text: FortiSwitch ACL hardware resource compaction windows.
choices.feedback: Switch TCAM operations do not govern SASE event visibility.

questions.stem: A FortiSASE change has a detailed audit comment. What remains unproven by that comment?

choices.text: That the log identifies the modified object and operator.
choices.feedback: The audit entry is designed to identify actor and object.

choices.text: That the configuration-audit gate was invoked successfully.
choices.feedback: The existence of the summary supports gate execution.

choices.text: That an administrator supplied a summary before submission.
choices.feedback: The comment is evidence of a submitted summary.

choices.text: That the new policy was enforced correctly for endpoints.
choices.feedback: An audit note does not attest to actual endpoint enforcement.

questions.stem: A FortiGate has no FortiGuard SLA preset catalog after a license lapse. Which prerequisite is relevant?

choices.text: A valid SD-WAN Underlay and Application Monitoring license.
choices.feedback: The database download/update requires this license.

choices.text: An enabled FortiPAM TOTP template with a shared key.
choices.feedback: PAM target OTP has no role in SLA catalog access.

choices.text: A FortiSIEM ClickHouse worker in each storage region.
choices.feedback: SIEM worker placement is unrelated to FortiGuard licensing.

choices.text: A FortiNAC portal HTTP rule that forwards probe requests.
choices.feedback: NAC portal rules do not authorize SLA database updates.

questions.stem: A FortiGuard SLA preset probe passes, but SaaS login fails. What does this observation mean?

choices.text: The SaaS authentication system must be working normally.
choices.feedback: Probe success does not test user authentication end-to-end.

choices.text: Probe success does not validate DNS/TLS/application login.
choices.feedback: Probe health is narrower than full application transaction success.

choices.text: The FortiGate automatically disables all other WAN members.
choices.feedback: A passing probe does not disable unrelated WAN members.

choices.text: The SD-WAN rule has necessarily chosen that WAN member.
choices.feedback: Rule matching and session selection must be verified separately.

questions.stem: An SD-WAN health-check CLI entry references a FortiGuard preset. Which parameters identify the feature?

choices.text: `set density-mode enable` and `execute acl key-compaction`.
choices.feedback: These settings govern FortiSwitch ACL resource handling.

choices.text: `set addke1` and `set childless-ike` on phase one.
choices.feedback: These settings control IPsec hybrid key exchanges.

choices.text: `set fortiguard enable` and `set fortiguard-name` values.
choices.feedback: These health-check fields select the FortiGuard SLA catalog entry.

choices.text: `set totp-length` and `set totp-duration` in a secret.
choices.feedback: These settings govern privileged target OTP generation.

questions.stem: Two branches use the same FortiGuard SLA preset but steer differently. What should be compared?

choices.text: Only the administrator who created each SD-WAN zone.
choices.feedback: Creator identity does not determine WAN forwarding decisions.

choices.text: Only the FortiAnalyzer archive quota on each appliance.
choices.feedback: Archive quota is not an SD-WAN steering input.

choices.text: Only the display names of the configured SLA checks.
choices.feedback: Identical names do not imply identical measured path quality.

choices.text: Probe results, member eligibility, thresholds and rule matches.
choices.feedback: Member measurements and rule selection explain path differences.

questions.stem: During an incident, a FortiNAC portal redirect works while FortiSASE policy edits require comments. Which conclusion avoids conflating the two controls?

choices.text: The portal handles HTTP requests; SASE gates administrator changes.
choices.feedback: These are distinct HTTP request and administrator-audit boundaries.

choices.text: Both mechanisms directly assign RADIUS VLANs to endpoints during authentication.
choices.feedback: Neither mechanism inherently assigns both systems' RADIUS VLANs.

choices.text: Both mechanisms negotiate post-quantum IKE key exchanges.
choices.feedback: Neither is an IKEv2 cryptographic negotiation feature.

choices.text: Both mechanisms prove all downstream application sessions succeed.
choices.feedback: Both can succeed while downstream services still fail.

questions.stem: A dashboard is empty after a change, and operators propose resetting the database. Which evidence-first comparison best separates FortiAnalyzer from FortiSIEM?

choices.text: Use the same archive quota number for both products.
choices.feedback: Different storage engines cannot be diagnosed from one quota.

choices.text: Check FAZ rolled files versus SIEM worker-to-shard persistence.
choices.feedback: FAZ file retention and SIEM region placement have distinct evidence.

choices.text: Disable MPSK on all access points before examining logs.
choices.feedback: WLAN keys are unrelated to both storage ingestion paths.

choices.text: Change FortiGate PQC groups to refresh the dashboard data.
choices.feedback: IKE KEM settings do not repair event storage visibility.
